The project

About

Mindscape is an experimental AI tool exploring a learning-first approach: make the concepts behind a task explicit, learn patterns from examples, and check the actions that follow. Our research combines structured knowledge, memory, and verified execution.

Research update · 12 October 2026

What Mindscape can demonstrate today

The project has grown from multiplication and Python repair into a shared cognitive kernel with three domain adapters. Existing learned models propose numerical transitions, code repairs and physical outcomes. Independent executors and scorers check what actually happens.

Mathematics

Neural transition learners compose local claims under declared procedural scaffolds. The target was not reached; the two integration examples both fail.

Python coding

Structured repair and verified training memories run through WASI. New-benchmark OOD success is 8/12; the strongest reference solves 9/12.

Read the evidence ↗

Physical dynamics

The complete V3 study exposed catastrophic motion divergence. V3.1 stabilizes finite rollouts, but fails improvement and calibration gates.

Read the evidence ↗

The latest milestone is reproducible integration, not a reasoning breakthrough. The mathematical study missed its target; coding concepts did not beat the strongest matched reference; physics stability research remains NO-GO for scaling. Future work should diagnose these failures before expanding training.

Our vision for
inspectable intelligence

We want to understand whether recording and controlling the process of solving a task can improve learning, structural generalization, and grounded execution.

Mindscape puts a learned policy inside an explicit system of observations, state, actions, events, results, and goals. Every executed step leaves evidence that can be inspected and replayed.

Our approachResearch report ›

An answer tells us what a model produced.
The process shows us what actually happened.

The problem we
are investigating

A correct-looking answer does not tell us whether a system executed the right steps, used reliable evidence, or reached the intended goal.

A model can describe a repair without producing a program that passes tests. It can predict an outcome without executing an action. A high score on familiar tasks can hide weak performance on unfamiliar structures.

We need to measure those differences explicitly. Otherwise, it is easy to confuse confident proposals with verified results, or the contribution of a learned policy with the work performed by its controller.

What was proposed?Action→Execution
What really happened?Prediction→Result
Does it generalize?Familiar→Unfamiliar

Different questions. Separate evidence.

How we are
approaching it

The policy proposes a bounded action. A controlled environment executes it, produces an actual result, and changes the state. The system records that transition, then checks whether the final outcome satisfies the goal.

In coding tasks, the model receives a broken repository, a specification, and visible tests. Trusted tools apply validated edits. Private tests assess the terminal program after the policy stops.

Working memory resets for every episode. Verified experience memory comes from executed training examples. Hypothetical plans remain separate from real results.

How we keep
the work grounded

We freeze protocols, preserve task identities and model hashes, retain unsuccessful runs, and bind results to recorded evidence.

Generated code executes inside a capability-limited WASI guest. Private evaluation evidence stays outside model observations. Execution and resource controls are enforced by trusted tools.

These safeguards bound execution and support scientific integrity. They are not a claim of comprehensive model alignment or formal security certification.

Safety and integrity

RESEARCH PRINCIPLES

Keep the evidence.
Keep the failures.
Keep the limits.

Predictions are hypothetical.
Execution produces actual results.
Unknown measurements stay unknown.

Where Mindscape began

The project began with decimal multiplication: a small environment that makes digit positions, carries, partial rows, and goal completion explicit. Later studies introduced learned numerical policies and tested how much success came from the policy, its representation, and deterministic action constraints.

The coding environment carries the same research questions into repositories, files, symbols, tests, and typed edits. A secondary SQLite environment tests interface portability; its model study remains deferred.

What remains scientifically unresolved

Mindscape’s central hypothesis is still being tested. The next work is to match supervision and interaction budgets, investigate structural OOD failures, test controllers with genuinely non-singleton choices, and extend telemetry and independent replication.

The current evidence supports bounded mechanisms and narrow software-repair observations. It does not establish general intelligence, reliable learned physical dynamics, broad model superiority, or a demonstrated benefit from dreaming.
